title: The George Buck album musicians and repertoire
summary: She names the players and notes only a couple of songs she had recorded before; she can slip in unusual material.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But anyway, Jack Howe on tenor and Johnny Haynes on bass and Tom Martin on drums. We got through this album easy enough but it was cold, the studio was cold. We were sitting around there with our overcoats on and of course Art Hodes took charge and conducted the band. It was very informal and we had a good time making this ablum and it was like a reunion, you know, being with Art Hodes and seeing him after all these years.

There are just a couple of things on this album that I have recorded before, "I've Got a Right to Sing the Blues," "He's Funny That Way," "The St. Louis Blues," but I had just obtained -- someone I had sort of been seeking around and trying to find the music to "We Just Couldn't Say Goodbye," and somebody had furnished me with a copy of it, so I said we would put this in the album and we called the album "We Just Couldn't Say Goodbye."

And so most of these things now -- see, this is how I get to throw some new things into my repertoire, by introducing one or two songs at a time. But this album is just out at the beginning of this year
